---
title: "Week 4 · Measuring disparities"
subtitle: "Textbook Chapter 4, Race and ethnicity"
---

**Skill this week:** measuring disparities and joining tables. By the end of the week you should be able to calculate a location quotient, interpret an index of dissimilarity, join a health table to boundaries by a key, and explain why a cluster needs a statistical test.

## Materials

::: {.week-card}
**[Slides](slides.qmd)**: categories, scale, location quotient, segregation, environmental justice, table joins, and HIV clustering. Press `S` to open the speaker notes.
:::

::: {.week-card}
**[Handout and cheat sheet](handout.qmd)**: the Week 4 formulas, a checklist for joins, and ArcGIS Online steps. A PDF version is linked on the handout page.
:::

- Chapter 4, Race and ethnicity
- Tanser F, Bärnighausen T, Cooke GS, Newell ML. Localized spatial clustering of HIV infections in a widely disseminated rural South African epidemic. *Int J Epidemiol.* 2009;38(4):1008-1016. [doi:10.1093/ije/dyp148](https://doi.org/10.1093/ije/dyp148)

## Map

Complete ArcGIS Online Exercises 4.1 Measuring spatial distribution with population ratios, 4.2 Measuring spatial distribution with the location quotient, 4.4 Income, race and ethnicity, and 4.5 Environmental justice. The links are at [esri.com/Human-Geography](https://www.esri.com/Human-Geography).

For more practice: Exercises 4.3 Tapestry segmentation and 4.6 The cultural landscape.

## Public health case

Within one relatively homogeneous rural population, local HIV prevalence ranged from 6% to 36%, with three statistically significant high-risk clusters along the national road.
